Every connected edge preserves exact alphabet support; therefore all alphabet sizes at lengths 2-5 reduce to finitely many support components on at most five letters. Complete enumerations, two-colourings, and augmenting-path perfect matchings certify all small support components except ternary length five; that 42-vertex graph has a 19-element independent set and an exact doubled-integer covering by twelve edges and six seven-cycles with cover two at every vertex and total doubled capacity 39, proving an integer upper bound 19. Summing binomial support types proves the universal formula. Explicit legal seven-cycle and common-prefix propagation show sharp nonbipartiteness for q>=3, n>=5. Both standalone programs were run from the package paths and returned their expected success markers. The finite graph computations are exhaustive only because of the proved support-preservation reduction.

value.rationale: The two-read deletion-reconstruction capacity on homopolymer-free strings is an operationally natural constrained coding invariant. The first sharp nonbinary deviation from half the available words occurs at exactly length five, with an all-q expression and a two-unit loss per alphabet triple. A nontrivial 42-vertex rational dual certificate establishes the defect and a seven-cycle demonstrates its structural source. This exact finite natural classification need not yield a large-block capacity theorem to be useful, and it is neither a mere relabeling of the unrestricted edge count nor a known-table recomputation.
